content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Thanks for sharing that. Before we get into any screens or features, I'd like to understand the *why* behind this, so we build the right thing.

A few questions to start:

1. **When this bookmark app is finished, what should be different from how you save links today?** What's frustrating or missing about your current way of doing it?

2. **Who is this for** — just you, or other people too?

3. When you picture "managing" bookmarks, what does *managing* mean to you — for example, finding a saved link again later, grouping them, sharing them, cleaning out old ones, or something else? What's the part that matters most?

You don't have to answer all of these formally — just tell me in your own words what you're hoping this will do for you.

It’s mainly for me. Right now my links are scattered and hard to find again, so I want one place where I can save a URL quickly and later retrieve it by searching or using tags.

“Managing” mostly means keeping useful details with each link, marking things to read later, and archiving links I want to keep without cluttering the main view. I’d also like the app to pick up the page title and other basic information automatically, while still letting me correct it or add my own notes. If I save the same link twice, I’d expect it to bring me back to the existing bookmark rather than create a duplicate.

content:
That's really clear — thank you. Let me play back what I understood to make sure I've got the direction right:

> **Your goal:** Right now your links are scattered and hard to find again. You want one place where you can save a URL quickly and reliably get back to it later — by searching or by tags. Beyond just storing the address, you want to keep useful details and your own notes with each link, mark some as "read later," and tuck away (archive) links you want to keep without cluttering your main view. When you save a link, the app should fill in the page title and basic info for you automatically, but let you correct it or add your own. And if you save a link you already have, it should take you back to the existing one instead of making a duplicate.

Two quick checks:

1. **Is that the right direction overall?** Anything I've overstated, understated, or missed?

2. Of everything you mentioned — quick saving, finding again (search/tags), notes/details, read-later, archiving, auto-filled info, no-duplicates — **is there one part that's the heart of it** for you? The thing that, if it didn't work well, would make the whole app not worth using?

And one more, about the shape of the app itself:

3. **What kind of app do you have in mind?** For example something you use in a web browser, on your phone, on your desktop, or in a terminal?

Yes, that’s the right direction. The heart of it is being able to find a saved link again quickly. Search should look through the address, title, description, and my notes without caring about capitalization, and tags should make it easy to narrow things down.

I picture this as a web app I can use in a browser. Saving should still feel quick, but good search and organization are what would make it worth using.

content:
We've now explored the whole picture — the everyday flows and the unusual moments — and your reactions have stopped changing the design. Here's the full scope that's settled:

**Saving**
- Paste a link and press Add; the app fills in the title and the site's summary automatically, in one panel where you review, add tags and your own note, then confirm — keeping saving quick.
- If a page can't be read automatically, you can still save it and fill in the details.
- An empty or invalid entry is politely refused; a bare address without `https://` is accepted.

**Each saved link**
- Shows a site icon, a clickable title that opens the page, the site's summary, your own note (separate, with simple lists/links), tags, and a small de-emphasised address.
- You can correct any of it anytime.

**Finding again (the heart)**
- Search spans address, title, summary and note together, ignoring capitalization, with matches highlighted.
- Power search: `#tag`, `"exact phrases"`, and `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` with parentheses (and those words act as plain text inside quotes); an incomplete query is flagged gently rather than guessed.
- Tags: added with suggestions to reuse spellings; filter by chips, narrowing to items with **all** chosen tags.

**Organising**
- Mark links **To read**; **Archive** to keep them out of the main list; each has its own view with friendly empty states.
- Re-saving a link you already have opens the existing one for editing — never a duplicate — and treats trailing-slash and http/https variants as the same, keeping the secure address.
- Sort by newest, recently updated, oldest, or title; a deliberate **default** in Settings, with the dropdown as a temporary override.

I've also noted for later: cleanly handling very long content and large collections (visual polish/performance), and an explicit "refresh details from the page" action — these are recorded and not part of this build.

**May I now start building this scope for real?** (That's the switch from exploring to implementation — I won't proceed without your go-ahead.)

This is a strong summary of what we’ve covered, but I’m not ready to call it the whole scope yet. A few important management needs are missing:

- I need to permanently delete a bookmark, clearly distinguished from reversible archiving.
- Editing should include the saved address itself, not only its title, summary, tags, and note.
- I need to select several bookmarks—or everything matching the current search/view—and add or remove tags, mark read or unread, archive, or delete them together.
- I’d like to save a useful combination of search terms and included or excluded tags as a reusable collection.
- The app should preserve a local copy of a page for later viewing; for a PDF, it should keep the PDF itself. Creating an Internet Archive copy should also be available.
- I need to import and export standard browser-bookmark HTML files, retaining titles, tags, and original dates.
- Settings should also cover things like font size and how many items are displayed.
- When collecting page details, include the real site icon and preview image where available.

Also, ordinary long titles, notes, and many tags wrapping cleanly is part of this build’s basic readability; performance work for genuinely large collections can remain later.

Please add these to the proposed scope before implementation begins.
